name: MUSE: A Memory-Utilizing and Self-Evolving Agent (Learning on the Job: An Experience-Driven, Self-Evolving Agent for Long-Horizon Tasks)
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2510.08002 (cs.CL; cs.AI), submitted 9 Oct 2025 (v1). DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2510.08002. No peer-reviewed venue identified as of the cutoff; DBLP id journals/corr/abs-2510-08002.
authors_affiliation: Cheng Yang (Central South University & Shanghai AI Laboratory), Xuemeng Yang, Licheng Wen (equal contribution; Shanghai AI Lab & Shanghai Innovation Institute), Daocheng Fu (Fudan University & Shanghai AI Lab), Jianbiao Mei, Rong Wu (Zhejiang University & Shanghai AI Lab), Pinlong Cai, Yufan Shen, Nianchen Deng, Botian Shi (corresponding; Shanghai AI Lab), Yu Qiao (Shanghai AI Lab), Haifeng Li (corresponding; Central South University). Primary affiliations: Central South University, Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, Fudan University, Shanghai Innovation Institute, Zhejiang University.
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/KnowledgeXLab/MUSE (ranks #1 on TheAgentCompany leaderboard https://the-agent-company.com/#/leaderboard; last updated Oct 16 2025, ~91 stars)
task_domain: LLM-agent decision-making on long-horizon real-world productivity tasks: cross-application computer-use (web browsing, code editing, shell, file/spreadsheet/PDF manipulation, chat/project-management tools). Spans web + code + general OS tool-use within a simulated software-company environment.
problem_setting: Interactive, multi-application, single primary agent operating in a fixed environment E (chat clients, cloud storage, project management, code editors, browsers, OS) executing actions via a minimal general-purpose toolset. Tasks are long-horizon productivity tasks (often >40 and up to >100 action steps, spanning two or more apps). The core challenge is gradient-free test-time learning ('learning on the job'): the backbone LLM (Gemini-2.5 Flash by default, also DeepSeek-V3) is NOT fine-tuned; instead a natural-language Memory Module is incrementally built from the agent's own trajectories so performance R(t) improves over repeated trials. The framework is multi-agent internally (a Planning-Execution PE Agent and a separate third-party Reflect Agent supervisor, both sharing the same toolset). Supervision is autonomous/self-supervised: the Reflect Agent self-judges sub-task success/failure (no human labels) via truthfulness, deliverable, and data-fidelity checks; TAC's official protocol provides scoring only for final evaluation, not as a training signal.
what_is_retrieved: Self-distilled, hierarchically organized experience at three abstraction levels: (1) Strategic Memory = high-level <Dilemma, Strategy/Resolution-Pattern> behavioral principles; (2) Procedural Memory = Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for sub-tasks, indexed by application then by SOP, capturing key analyses/precautions/core parameters/operational steps; (3) Tool Memory = per-tool static descriptions + dynamic post-use instructions ('muscle memory'). The agent actively retrieves Procedural-Memory SOP content on demand; Strategic and Tool memories are always loaded into the prompt rather than retrieved.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING/episodic self-written memory. The retrievable store (the Memory Module M = {M_strat, M_proc, M_tool}) is entirely self-generated from the agent's own past trajectories and grows across tasks/iterations; there is no static external corpus/KB/API doc store being retrieved. (Memory can be frozen for the final TAC full-benchmark evaluation after 3 continual-learning iterations, but it is grown online during learning.)
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Neither a fixed top-k ranking nor an explicit minimal-complete-set objective. Procedural-Memory retrieval is agent-initiated, on-demand fetching of specific SOP contents (the agent queries relevant SOPs by application/item when uncertain), so it is a precision-driven, variable-size lookup rather than a ranked top-k; the goal is to recover the relevant procedural guidance for the current sub-task, not to optimize a Recall@k metric.
retrieval_unit: workflow-routine / procedural SOP (problem-solution-style 'case' for a sub-task) is the primary retrieved unit (full content of an SOP: preconditions, steps, notes for a given application function). Secondary always-loaded units are guideline-rules (Strategic Memory <Dilemma,Strategy> principles) and tool-API usage notes (Tool Memory descriptions + dynamic instructions).
index_source: Growing memory, online/test-time-induced (hybrid two-stage construction). SOPs and other memories are induced at test time from the agent's own successful sub-task trajectories: added immediately after a successful sub-task for instant reuse, then globally refined (dedup/generalization) after the whole task. No offline pretraining of the store; it is built and refined during deployment.
index_structure_topology: Hierarchical for Procedural Memory: indexed first by application (related platforms/APIs), then a second-level SOP index per sub-task (application -> function -> SOP). Crucially, a lightweight SOP INDEX is separated from heavy SOP CONTENT (p = (index_p, content_p)). Strategic Memory is a flat concise set of <Dilemma,Strategy> key-value principles; Tool Memory is keyed per tool. No dense vector index or knowledge graph is used for the SOPs; retrieval is via an application/item-keyed lookup tool (access_guide / a_mem).
retriever_type: LLM-as-retriever / agent-initiated tool-based lookup. The PE Agent invokes a dedicated memory-retrieval tool (access_guide, a_mem) with a batch request of application/item names to fetch the relevant SOP content; selection is driven by the agent's reasoning over the lightweight SOP index rather than by BM25/dense embedding similarity. Strategic and Tool memories are not retrieved (always prompt-loaded).
retriever_learning_signal: none (no trained retriever). Retrieval/selection is performed by the off-the-shelf backbone LLM reasoning over the loaded SOP index and choosing which SOP content to fetch via a tool call; there is no contrastive training, LM-feedback retriever, preference/Bradley-Terry, RL, or value-based retrieval policy. (What IS learned online is the memory CONTENT, not the retriever.)
query_construction: Agent-formed intent query: the PE Agent, given the current sub-task st_i = (desc_i, goal_i) and the loaded SOP index, formulates a batch request naming the relevant application(s) and item(s) (e.g., batch_requests={'RocketChat': ['Login','Create Channel']}) to pull SOP content. Prompt engineering encourages the agent to query for relevant experience at the start of each sub-task and whenever uncertain. No embedding-based query vector; query = LLM-selected app/item keys.
query_granularity: sub-task / step-level (proactive, on-demand). Procedural retrieval is keyed to the current sub-task and can be issued at any point during execution when the agent faces uncertainty (not a single one-shot at t=0 for the whole task, and not a fixed per-step schedule). Strategic/Tool memory injection is task-level (loaded once at initialization).
when_to_retrieve: active / agent-initiated (uncertainty-triggered, on-demand) for Procedural Memory: the agent proactively queries detailed SOPs 'when facing uncertainty', mimicking a human expert consulting past cases; prompt-encouraged at sub-task start. By contrast Strategic and Tool memories are one-shot loaded at initialization (always-on, not retrieved).
retrieval_trigger_signal: agent-initiated request driven by the agent's own assessment of uncertainty: the PE Agent decides within its ReAct (Thought-Action-Observation) loop to emit a memory-retrieval action (a_mem / access_guide) when it needs decision support, and is prompted to prioritize querying at the beginning of each sub-task. Not token-confidence, attention/uncertainty scores, a learned complexity classifier, or reflection tokens.
reranking: None. There is no cross-encoder, RRF, hierarchy-aware, or instruction-tuned reranking stage; the agent directly fetches the SOP content(s) it selects from the index via the lookup tool.
retrieved_context_refinement: Index-content separation as the main efficiency mechanism: only the lightweight SOP index is loaded at startup; full SOP content is loaded on demand (progressive disclosure), keeping context small. Beyond this, retrieved SOP content is used largely as-is; refinement (dedup, generalization, merging) is applied at WRITE/consolidation time (post-task global refinement) rather than as a post-retrieval distillation of fetched items. Tool Memory's dynamic instruction is appended with the observation to guide the next action.
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation + procedural guidance reuse. Retrieved SOP content is injected into the PE Agent's ReAct context to guide composing primitive tool actions into the workflow for the sub-task (case/SOP reuse). Strategic Memory principles are loaded into the system prompt to steer global strategy; Tool Memory static descriptions are in the system prompt and dynamic instructions are returned with each observation to guide the next action. No fine-tuning or latent-token injection; all knowledge is natural-language in-context (making it LLM-agnostic/transferable).
planning_integration: retrieve-then-plan/act at the sub-task level inside a 'Plan-Execute-Reflect-Memorize' loop. The PE Agent decomposes the task into an ordered sub-task queue Q, and for each sub-task first queries Procedural Memory for relevant SOP guidance, then runs a memory-enhanced ReAct loop; after each sub-task the Reflect Agent evaluates and the PE Agent adaptively replans/updates Q. Retrieval is interleaved within sub-task execution (the agent can re-query mid-execution). Not MCTS/tree-search; planning is iterative queue maintenance with reflect-driven replanning and a retry that explicitly disables Procedural Memory to encourage exploration of novel methods.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-tool-call within a sub-task rollout: memory retrieval is one possible action in the agent's (Thought, Action, Observation) ReAct iteration, issued on demand (typically at sub-task start and when uncertain). It is therefore finer than per-answer/per-task but coarser than a fixed per-token schedule; the natural unit is the sub-task and the individual tool-call step.
retrieved_item_representation: Structured natural-language notes. Procedural Memory SOPs are free-text structured guides (Application | Function | Preconditions/Steps/Notes). Strategic Memory is <Dilemma/Principle, Description/Strategy> pairs. Tool Memory is per-tool Description + Instruction text. Everything is human-readable natural language (not raw trajectories injected verbatim, not executable programs, not latent/soft tokens).
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Multi-level by design: (1) distilled high-level strategy/principle (Strategic Memory, macro behavioral paradigms); (2) reusable procedural workflow/SOP for tool-sequence combinations (Procedural Memory); (3) single-tool usage guidance ('muscle memory', Tool Memory). Raw action trajectories are explicitly converted into these structured abstractions to enhance reusability and reduce redundant exploration.
noise_robustness_mechanism: (1) Independent third-party Reflect Agent supervises execution to suppress hallucinations (e.g., false 'task complete' beliefs) via an ordered checklist: Truthfulness Verification (ground conclusions in real environmental feedback), Deliverable Verification, Data Fidelity; using trajectory referencing + active verification (proactively re-interacting with the environment to cross-check). (2) Only SUCCESSFUL trajectories become SOPs, and post-task global refinement deduplicates/generalizes/merges to maintain quality and prevent context bloat. (3) The retry mechanism disables Procedural Memory when existing knowledge is 'erroneous or inapplicable', guarding against stale/incorrect retrieved guidance. (4) Tool-memory notes warn the agent that guides may not match current UI and to prioritize adaptive exploration on discrepancies.
memory_type: Procedural + workflow + strategic experiential memory (hierarchical, natural-language, long-term). Composite M = {Strategic (semantic/strategic guidelines), Procedural (SOP workflows), Tool (per-tool procedural notes)}; not a vector-embedding store, not a knowledge graph, not latent.
write_back: Yes. After each successful sub-task the Reflect Agent distills the trajectory into a new SOP (p_new) added to Procedural Memory; after the whole task it distills higher-level Strategic Memory (<Dilemma,Resolution-Pattern>) and Tool Memory, then performs a global refinement/integration of all three memory types.
online_growth: Yes (during learning). The Memory Module grows continuously across sub-tasks/tasks/iterations at test time (3 continual-learning iterations over an 18-task set, carrying knowledge forward). For the final TAC full-175-task evaluation the memory is FROZEN after those 3 iterations, demonstrating zero-shot generalization, but the mechanism is online-growing by construction.
write_back_trigger: Two-stage, reflective and outcome-gated: (a) immediately after a sub-task, on success the Reflect Agent writes a new SOP to Procedural Memory (and on failure generates a failure-cause report R_fail that triggers replanning, not a stored memory item); (b) after the entire task completes, a post-task distillation writes/updates Strategic and Tool memories from the full trajectory and globally refines all memory. Writing is autonomous/self-judged (no human validation in the default fully-autonomous setting; the architecture also permits optional human add/delete/modify/query).
failure_experience_usage: Largely success-only for persistent memory: SOPs are summarized only from SUCCESSFUL sub-task trajectories. Failures are used transiently/diagnostically (failure-cause analysis R_fail feeds immediate replanning and a memory-free retry to encourage exploration) and inform the distilled Strategic <Dilemma, Resolution-Pattern> principles (which encode how dilemmas were overcome), but failed trajectories are not stored as standalone negative/contrastive memory items. The Discussion notes contrasting successful vs failed trajectories as future work.
memory_evolution_update: Refine-and-merge, not pure append-only. Procedural Memory: SOPs are added immediately, then post-task global refinement performs deduplication and generalization. Strategic Memory: 'updated, merged, and refined after each task, always maintaining a concise size'. Tool Memory: updated by the Reflect Agent after each task. The whole module undergoes a periodic 'integrate new and old knowledge, eliminate redundancy, generalize common patterns' upgrade (dedup-merge + generalize + refine-overwrite), keeping size bounded.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/selection is performed by the off-the-shelf LLM reasoning (prompt-encouraged tool calls), not an RL-/value-optimized or otherwise trained retrieval policy. There is no M-MDP soft Q-learning or learned ranker; the learning happens in the memory content, not in a retrieval policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Cross-MODEL sharing rather than cross-agent. Because memory is stored in natural language, it is explicitly LLM-agnostic: experience accumulated by one model can be transferred to another (validated by transferring Gemini-2.5-Flash-accumulated memory to DeepSeek-V3). Internally it is a two-agent system (PE + Reflect) sharing one Memory Module, not a population of agents with shared memory; there is no multi-agent collective memory across heterogeneous frameworks.
benchmarks: TheAgentCompany (TAC) (Xu et al. 2024): 175 tasks across six employee roles (HR, PM, SDE, DS/Data Science, Finance, Admin/BizMaster) in a simulated software company (RocketChat, GitLab, Plane, ownCloud, etc.). Subsets used: T_cl (18 tasks, continual learning, all six roles); T_hard (12 hard tasks where strong models near-zero). NPCs powered by GPT-4o; visual extractor uses GPT-4o.
benchmark_family: web + code + decision-making productivity / computer-use agent benchmark (TheAgentCompany family). Closest to web (WebArena-style) and code (SWE-style) but specifically a long-horizon cross-application productivity benchmark; not QA/multi-hop, embodied, tool-retrieval (ToolBench), memory (LoCoMo), or decision-RL (D4RL).
baselines: On TAC full 175: OWL-RolePlay (GPT-4o + o3-mini); OpenHands (Gemini-1.5-Pro, Gemini-2.0-Flash, Gemini-2.5-Pro); OpenHands-Versa (Claude-3.7-Sonnet, Claude-4-Sonnet, the previous SOTA). On T_hard: OpenHands-Versa (Claude-4-Sonnet), OpenHands (Gemini-2.5-Pro), plus MUSE w/o memory. Open-source comparison (T_cl): OpenHands with Llama-3.1-405B, Llama-3.3-70B, Qwen-2.5-72B vs MUSE+DeepSeek-V3. Internal baselines: MUSE w/o Memory Module, and No-Reflection variant.
key_metrics: TAC official protocol: partial completion score S_partial = 0.5*(Completed_ckpt/Total_ckpt) + 0.5*S_full (S_full in {0,1}); aggregate checkpoint score S_ckpt (completed checkpoints / total checkpoints across all tasks); PCR = Perfect Completion Rate (fraction fully solved). Reported as averages over tasks (5 runs averaged for continual-learning).
headline_result: New SOTA on TAC full 175-task benchmark with a lightweight Gemini-2.5-Flash: Avg S_partial = 51.78% (S_ckpt = 59.92%, 465/776 checkpoints, PCR = 41.14%), the first agent to exceed 50% S_partial on TAC and ~20% relative improvement over the previous SOTA OpenHands-Versa + Claude-4-Sonnet (S_partial 43.19%, S_ckpt 50.52%, PCR 33.14%). Memory was learned from only ~10% of tasks (the 18-task T_cl set) and frozen for evaluation.
ablations: (1) Continual learning (T_cl, 18 tasks, 5 runs): both S_ckpt and S_partial grow monotonically over 3 iterations; final round beats the memory-less baseline by >10%. (2) Generalization (T_hard, 12 tasks): MUSE+Gemini-2.5-Flash w/o memory already S_partial 23.65% (S_ckpt 30.51%, 18/59 ckpt) vs OpenHands-Versa+Claude-4-Sonnet 2.00% and OpenHands+Gemini-2.5-Pro 3.00%; adding pre-learned (frozen) memory raises MUSE to S_partial 33.41% (S_ckpt 40.68%, 24/59) -> zero-shot transfer of memory. (3) Reflect Agent ablation (T_cl, both w/o memory): No-Reflection 43.21% S_partial (S_ckpt 63.53%) vs MUSE 55.85% (S_ckpt 66.12%) -> reflection is indispensable. (4) Cross-model / open-source (T_cl): MUSE+DeepSeek-V3 w/o memory 28.01% S_partial (beats OpenHands open-source: Llama-3.1-405B 9.78%, Llama-3.3-70B 5.84%, Qwen-2.5-72B 6.50%); MUSE+DeepSeek-V3 w/ (Gemini-learned) memory 36.75% -> memory is model-agnostic and transferable.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task metrics (S_partial, S_ckpt, PCR) are reported; no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG/completeness) are reported separately, since retrieval here is agent-initiated on-demand memory lookup rather than a ranked-retrieval benchmark.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Mostly outcome, with process granularity via checkpoints. S_partial and S_ckpt give partial-progress (intermediate checkpoint) credit beyond binary full completion, so intermediate progress is scored. The paper also gives qualitative process analysis (two case studies on adaptive multi-step strategies, ~20 sub-tasks / >100 actions), but does not report quantitative reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise retrieval-accuracy metrics. Step counts/latency/token cost are not tabulated.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Qualitatively strong but not quantified in money/tokens/latency. The central efficiency claim is matching/beating much stronger models (Claude-4-Sonnet, Gemini-2.5-Pro) using only the lightweight Gemini-2.5-Flash, and reducing redundant exploration by reusing structured memory (pruning the decision space, focusing on effective solutions). Context efficiency is achieved by index-content separation (load only the SOP index; fetch content on demand) and a concise, refined memory. The paper does not report retrieval-call counts, API cost, latency/speedup, or token-savings numbers (max N=20 actions per sub-task attempt; one retry).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Budget-conscious via progressive disclosure: only the lightweight SOP index is loaded at startup; full SOP content is fetched on demand by the agent (no fixed-k or reranked-then-truncated cap). Strategic Memory is deliberately kept concise (merged/refined to a small size) and Tool static descriptions are loaded at init. Per-sub-task attempt action budget N=20 (with one retry). No explicit token cap or fixed top-k for memory items reported.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (primary research paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses the existing TheAgentCompany benchmark, 175 Docker-image tasks; partial-credit checkpoint grading with LLM-assisted graders). Authors curate two subsets from TAC (T_cl 18 moderate-difficulty tasks; T_hard 12 near-zero-score tasks), manually inspected for correctness and balanced across the six roles, but construct no new benchmark.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes (on-demand SOP/procedural lookup by application/item via a memory tool), Reuse: yes (retrieved SOPs/strategies/tool-notes injected to guide ReAct execution), Revise: yes (Reflect Agent verifies/replans; retry disables memory to discover novel methods; post-task global refinement generalizes/merges experiences), Retain: yes (successful sub-task trajectories distilled into new SOPs immediately, plus post-task Strategic/Tool memory writes and integration)].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself as experience-driven, self-evolving agent memory / test-time learning ('learn on the job'), drawing on cognitive-science memory taxonomies; it does NOT cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner or use the term 'case-based reasoning'. It does analogize Procedural-Memory consultation to 'how human experts consult past cases', realizing CBR-like Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain under a memory framing (lineage near ExpeL/AWM/Memp).
tool_document_engineering: Tool descriptions are learned/engineered as Tool Memory: each tool has a Static Description (loaded at init explaining core functionality) and a Dynamic Instruction (returned with the observation after use, guiding the next action), and Tool Memory is updated/refined by the Reflect Agent after each task from successful usage (i.e., experience-augmented tool docs with usage caveats), rather than raw docstrings or synthetic-query-augmented embeddings.
index_content_separation: Yes - this is a defining feature. Procedural Memory SOPs are stored as p = (index_p, content_p); only the lightweight index of all SOPs is loaded into context at sub-task start, and the full content is fetched on demand via a dedicated tool (a_mem / access_guide). This SOP-index-then-content progressive disclosure minimizes context overhead while enabling low-cost experience reuse within the LLM's context limit.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Partially applicable: the agent uses a minimal general-purpose toolset (browser operator built on the browser-use framework, code interpreter / run_python_code, shell / run_cmd, GPT-4o vision extractor, memory retriever access_guide) rather than a large live external API registry; there is no RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP tool-store with CRUD auto-sync. The Procedural-Memory SOP store IS dynamically updated (added/refined) during operation, but it indexes self-induced procedures, not third-party tools.
tool_dependency_awareness: Partial/implicit. Procedural SOPs and Tool dynamic instructions encode operational sequencing (e.g., 'always follow a click with browser_update', 'after input locate and click Save/Submit'), capturing prerequisite/next-action dependencies between tool calls; but there is no explicit inter-tool dependency graph, bipartite KG, or dependency-aware reranking.
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted adaptation + execution-feedback-driven revision. Retrieved SOPs are not copied verbatim: tool notes explicitly tell the agent guides 'may not match current UI; adapt as needed' and to prioritize adaptive exploration on discrepancies. The Reflect Agent's verification drives replanning, and a memory-free retry lets the agent discover novel methods when stored knowledge is wrong/inapplicable. Post-task distillation generalizes the adapted solution back into refined memory.
builds_on: ReAct (Yao et al. 2023) for the Thought-Action-Observation loop; procedural/experience-memory line ExpeL (Zhao et al. 2024, trajectory->NL insights/rules), Agent Workflow Memory (Wang et al. 2024, reusable workflows), Memp (Fang et al. 2025, learnable lifelong procedural memory); memory-management work Mem0 (Chhikara et al. 2025) and MemInsight (Salama et al. 2025); Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023) and SAGE (Liang et al. 2025) for self-reflection; skill/toolset self-evolution (Voyager, OS-Copilot, Iterative Experience Refinement, Agent-KB, Alita). Built on the browser-use framework for browser actions; evaluated on TheAgentCompany (Xu et al. 2024); backbone Gemini-2.5 (Comanici et al. 2025) and DeepSeek-V3.
contrasts_with: Static, test-time-frozen LLM agents (cannot learn from experience); massive-API tool agents like ToolLLM (Qin et al. 2023) and Gorilla (Patil et al. 2024) - MUSE instead uses a minimal toolset and learns to compose primitives; embedding/vector-DB or knowledge-graph memory stores (e.g., FAISS-, Neo4j-based) - MUSE uses natural-language, application-keyed SOP index with index-content separation; prior procedural-memory methods (ExpeL, AWM, Memp) validated mainly on short-horizon text/web benchmarks (HotpotQA, ALFWorld, WebShop, WebArena, Mind2Web) that lack TAC's long-horizon cross-application complexity; fine-tuning and sparse-reward RL approaches (deemed intractable / hard to reward for >100-step productivity tasks).
lineage: Group F (decision/memory/experience-driven self-evolving agents). A 2025 procedural/strategic experience-memory framework extending the ExpeL -> Agent Workflow Memory -> Memp lineage of self-distilled, test-time-learned agent memory. Distinctive contributions: (a) a hierarchical three-level Memory Module (Strategic / Procedural / Tool) at differing abstraction levels; (b) SOP index-content separation enabling low-cost, agent-initiated on-demand procedural retrieval; (c) a PE + independent Reflect dual-agent 'Plan-Execute-Reflect-Memorize' loop with autonomous self-verification; (d) natural-language, LLM-agnostic memory enabling cross-model experience transfer; (e) new SOTA on the long-horizon cross-application productivity benchmark TheAgentCompany with a lightweight backbone.
